content_html_sanitized:
There are various myths and theories about how “420” came to symbolize and then celebrate using “marijuana,” a.k.a. cannabis.

See 420 (cannabis culture)

However, whatever the origin, all of them necessarily involve breaking the law, because the plant has been illegal federally since 1937, and it was illegal under various state laws for most of that time. Now it is more or less legal in 24 states, plus D.C., for recreational use and more or less legal in 39 states for medical use.

And these laws were, and to a degree still are, vigorously and often viciously enforced. There have been over 30 million arrests since 1972, when Nixon’s Shafer Commission https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shafer_Commission recommended that it be decriminalized.

And even now there are still over 200,000 arrests per year, about which we hear almost nothing. The failure of America’s “free press” to report on the tens of millions of arrests, and the prohibitionist denial that many people were being arrested, actually undermined marijuana prohibition. Stealth terrorism is not really very effective.

And remember, almost no one smoked it in 1937. Almost 22% of Americans used marijuana in the last year. Roughly half have used it at some point. More Americans use marijuana daily than use alcohol daily.

Another measure of the clandestine nature of the culture that developed around cannabis can be found in the fact that there are over 1,200 slang words for it. Absolutely amazing. List of slang names for cannabis

And then there was/is D.A.R.E., the “anti-drug” organization founded by Daryl Gates, the disastrous Los Angeles Police Chief.

And, Giuliani’s Police State – Like the Marijuana Prohibition That He Loves – Is a Counterproductive Fraud. 3 Articles.

Whatever happened to Rudy?

And “I like DARE. DARE gives kids the curiosity factor which leads them into finding one of the best plants on earth!”

And, I remember a cartoon from way back with a little boy at the breakfast table, looking suspiciously at a bowl of cereal and at his mother, saying, “You lied to us about marijuana. How do we know you didn’t lie to us about granola?”

Or heroin, or cocaine, or meth, or fentanyl, or…

Recently, some of the leading publications in the U.S. have published articles about the dangers of the new potent cannabis which they intend to be a warning and/or an incentive to restore cannabis prohibition to its previous glory.

I will be writing more about this later this week.

Of course, they would deny this, but ironically it will probably have the opposite effect, at least on those they are supposedly trying to protect. That’s the way it has worked for the last fifty years.

“WOW! It says right here that the new marijuana is much better than it used to be. Far out! See you at 420!”
